title: EIGEN: Enabling Efficient 3DIC Interconnect with Heterogeneous Dual-Layer Network-on-Active-Interposer
problem: Chiplet-based 3DIC systems using active interposers struggle with heterogeneous and high-load inter-chiplet network traffic patterns because their interconnects are tightly coupled to top-die designs, preventing flexible topology adaptation and causing high latency and traffic congestion.
motivation: As AI accelerators, CPUs, and GPUs are integrated via chiplets on active interposers for high-performance computing, rigid monolithic NoC designs cannot efficiently handle the heterogeneous traffic demands of mixed compute fabrics at scale.
method: EIGEN implements a heterogeneous dual-layer interconnect on the active interposer: an application-aware switch-programmable layer (AspLayer) for static topology optimization and a dynamic packet-routing layer (DynLayer) for adaptive traffic management. A reinforcement learning (RL)-based path routing framework is trained with a state space covering topology, network, and memory metrics, with reward defined as the product of average packet latency and link utilization. The two layers cooperate to route inter-chiplet traffic with reduced hops and congestion.
key_novelty: A dual-layer active-interposer NoC that separates static topology programmability from dynamic adaptive routing, coordinated by an RL-based framework trained on combined latency-utilization reward.
contributions: EIGEN heterogeneous dual-layer Network-on-Active-Interposer architecture (AspLayer + DynLayer)
RL-based path routing framework for dual-layer inter-chiplet communication optimization
Up to 67.16% latency reduction and 53.89% hop reduction vs SOTA chiplet interconnects
Scalability demonstrated from 4x4 to 32x32 chiplet configurations with consistent improvements

metrics.speedup: Up to 11.21% runtime reduction vs SOTA
metrics.other: Up to 67.16% latency reduction, 53.89% hop reduction; scalable from 4x4 to 32x32 chiplets

limitations: The RL routing framework's training convergence and generalization to unseen workload mixes at larger scales are not fully discussed.
primary_theme: dual-layer RL-guided network-on-active-interposer for chiplet systems
